name: Increment/Decrement Operators (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that performs increment/decrement operations on variable a (with initial value of 4) and variable b (with initial value of 5) and prints the following output as the result of these operations:\n-1\n3

comments.content: We define variable a and set its initial value to 4.
We define variable b and set its initial value to 5.
The expression in this println statement produces the first output. The subtraction operator uses original value of variables a (i.e., 4) and b (i.e., 5), thus generating the result of -1.

a++ evaluates to 4 and then increments variable a by 1. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 4.
b-- evaluates to 5 and then decrements variable b by 1. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 5.
Note that when we have post-increment/post-decrement operator, the variable gets incremented/decremented by 1, but the original value of that variable will be used in the statement.
The expression in this println statement produces the second output. The subtraction operator uses value of variables a and b after the pre-increment and pre-decrement operations are performed.

++a evaluates to 6 because, when program reaches here, variable a holds 5 and it gets incremented by 1 before the left-hand side of the subtraction operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 6.
--b evaluates to 3 because, when program reaches here, variable b holds 4 and it gets decremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the subtraction operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 3.
Note that when we have pre-increment/pre-decrement operator, the variable gets incremented/decremented by 1, and the updated value of that variable will be used in the statement.
